record.original_question: Let H be a pr-graph, meaning a br-graph that is switching-equivalent to a graph with no pure blue edges. Let B_H := B x H be its bipartite resolution, where B is the purple K_2, so B_H has the parity-flip automorphism (i, v) -> (1 - i, v). A bipartite-min ordering of B_H is an ordering on each partite set that satisfies the underbar property, and it is special if every vertex has all neighbors joined by purple edges before its other neighbors. Is it true that B_H has a special bipartite-min ordering if and only if it has a special bipartite-min ordering that is parity-symmetric, i.e. commutes with the parity flip?

evidence.quote: A br-graph that is switching-equivalent to a graph with no pure blue edges is a pr-graph (for purple-red).

For a br-graph H, the bipartite resolution of H is BH := B x H. It is a bipartite br-graph with partite sets pi_B^-1(0) and pi_B^-1(1), so we call i = pi_B((i, v)) the parity of a vertex (i, v) and call the map f_p : (i, v) -> (1 - i, v), which is clearly an automorphism of BH, the parity flip map. A polymorphism phi of BH is parity-symmetric if it commutes with the parity flip map.
An ordering of the vertices of a bipartite graph H with partite sets U and V is a bipartite-min ordering if for any a, b in U and a', b' in V, the underbar property (2) holds.

Given a pr-graph H with a (bipartite-)min ordering of the underlying graph, a vertex is special if all its neighbours via purple edges come before its other neighbours. The ordering is a special (bipartite-)min ordering if all vertices are special.
Conjecture 1.4. For a pr-graph H, BH has a special bipartite-min ordering if and only if it has a parity-symmetric one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A br-graph is a finite simple graph in which every edge is coloured either blue or red (a "blue-red graph"). Two br-graphs on the same vertex set are switching-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by selecting a subset S of vertices and swapping the colours (blue ↔ red) of every edge with exactly one endpoint in S. A br-graph H is called a pr-graph (purple-red) if it is switching-equivalent to a br-graph that has no blue edges; in that case the edges in the original presentation are classified, after a fixed switching to remove blue edges, as either purple (edges that became "neutral" through switching, i.e. the unchanged edges that exist in both colourings) or red.

Let B denote the "purple K_2": the graph on the two-element vertex set {0,1} with a single edge between 0 and 1, coloured purple. For a br-graph H, define its bipartite resolution
   B_H := B × H,
where × is the categorical (tensor) product of edge-coloured graphs: the vertex set is {0,1} × V(H), and (i,u)(j,v) is an edge of colour c precisely when i ≠ j and uv is an edge of H of colour c. Then B_H is a bipartite br-graph with partite sets P_0 = {0} × V(H) and P_1 = {1} × V(H). The parity of a vertex (i,v) is i, and the parity flip is the automorphism
   f_p : (i,v) ↦ (1−i, v)
of B_H.

A bipartite-min ordering of B_H is a pair of linear orders, one on P_0 and one on P_1, such that for all a,b in P_0 and a',b' in P_1, if a < b and a' < b', and if both ab' and ba' are edges, then aa' is an edge whose colour is "smaller-or-equal" (in the prescribed sense for br-graphs) than both ab' and ba'; this is the standard underbar condition for bipartite-min orderings of edge-coloured graphs.

Given a bipartite-min ordering of B_H, a vertex x is called special if every neighbour of x joined to x by a purple edge precedes (in the order on the opposite partite set) every neighbour of x joined to x by a non-purple edge. The ordering is a special bipartite-min ordering if every vertex of B_H is special.

A bipartite-min ordering of B_H is parity-symmetric if it commutes with the parity flip f_p, i.e. for all u,v ∈ V(H), (0,u) < (0,v) in the order on P_0 if and only if (1,u) < (1,v) in the order on P_1.

Question. Let H be a pr-graph. Prove or disprove: B_H admits a special bipartite-min ordering if and only if B_H admits a parity-symmetric special bipartite-min ordering.
artifact.status_search_result: No public sources were found that directly resolve this equivalence for parity-symmetric special bipartite-min orderings of bipartite resolutions of pr-graphs; the problem appears to be a specialized open question in the CSP/polymorphism literature on edge-coloured graphs, with no announced solution available.
